title: [NatWest demo] Payments - group related notable events
description:
Roll up notable events from BOTH the Splunk Observability detectors (forwarded via the o11y -> ITSI bridge correlation search) AND the Splunk ES correlation searches (excessive declines per tier, Madrid p95 latency breach, every chaos inject/clear, off-window chaos compliance overlay, SPA network connection changes, api-gateway 5xx rate, per-service p99 SLO breaches, ledger-service JDBC error storms, settlement-service consumer idle) into a single Episode per service per 30-minute window. The demo's story: detection from spans + detection from the banking audit log + detection from the chaos audit log + browser-side audit signals are independent signals about ONE incident. Without a grouping policy each signal opens a separate ticket; with this policy Episode Review shows the operator a single Episode with the attached notables, which is the desired SOC-on-stage flow.

Coverage matrix (which orig_source value each correlation search uses):
  - Splunk Observability Cloud      <- o11y_to_itsi.json (detector firings forwarded via webhook bridge)
  - Splunk ES - payments audit      <- payments_excessive_declines_by_tier.json
  - Splunk ES - chaos audit         <- chaos_injection_audit.json + chaos_off_change_window.json
  - Splunk ES - payments OTel       <- payments_madrid_latency_breach.json + payments_api_gateway_5xx_breach.json + payments_service_latency_slo_breach.json + payments_ledger_jdbc_errors.json + payments_settlement_consumer_idle.json
  - Splunk ES - SPA network audit   <- spa_network_connection_changed.json

Group mechanic:
  split_by_field = service                     (every notable carries 'service'='<L2 tile>')
  episode breaks  = 1800s with no new notable  (30 minutes of silence)
  on break + >=1 event -> resolve              (auto-closed)

IMPORTANT - filter field is 'orig_source', NOT 'source'. ITSI's event
generator automatically overwrites the user-supplied 'source' (set by
'action.itsi_event_generator.param.source = $result.source$' in the
correlation search) with the saved-search name (e.g. '[NatWest demo]
Chaos injection audit') at notable-creation time, and moves the
original value to 'orig_source'. Filtering on 'source' would never
match our intended source classification; always use 'orig_source' on
the policy + on any glass-table or Episode Review query that wants to
pivot by 'where the notable came from'.

Schema is the ITSI 4.20+ shape: criteria/actions are now arrays of typed items with an explicit condition, not the older flat clause/condition pairs. This file is consumed by scripts/lib/itsi_bootstrap.py which POSTs it to SA-ITOA/event_management_interface/notable_event_aggregation_policy (NOT itoa_interface - that endpoint 404s for this object type).

Follow-up: on the live tenant the policy is registered and reads back enabled (disabled=0), but the ITSI notable-event aggregator does not materialise grouped alerts into index=itsi_grouped_alerts for our notables, so the 'Active payments episodes' panel will read zero until the aggregator picks the policy up after a Splunk app restart (or until ITSI's internal aggregator schedule fires for our security group). Notables themselves continue to surface fine in the 'Active payments incident -- notable events' panel and in Episode Review's notable-event view, which is the primary demo signal. Re-validate by hitting Configuration -> Event Management -> Aggregation Policies in the UI and clicking Save to nudge the engine if grouping is needed live.
group_description: Grouped from notable events across sources Splunk Observability Cloud, Splunk ES - payments audit, Splunk ES - chaos audit, Splunk ES - payments OTel.

rules.title: Resolve orphaned singleton episodes after 5 minutes
rules.description: A service-axis episode with only one notable and no follow-on events for 5 minutes is noise (e.g. a lone audit correlation before the chaos cascade arrives). Auto-resolve so Episode Review stays focused on multi-signal incidents.

rules.title: Resolve episode when broken with at least one event
rules.description: When the 30-minute pause triggers a break AND the episode received at least one notable, flip status to Resolved. Avoids carry-over tickets when the underlying chaos has already cleared.
